status_reasoning: Reviewers explicitly state that 'the data are presented clearly and precisely, and they unambiguously demonstrate that granule cells are multimodal' and that 'the main conclusions of this study are strongly supported.' This directly affirms the core finding of ECN-BPN convergence onto individual granule cells and the mapping of this convergence across cerebellar cortex.

Reviewers explicitly affirm that the findings 'unambiguously demonstrate that granule cells are multimodal, supporting the predictions of the Marr–Albus theory of cerebellar function.' This directly validates the claims about informing the multimodality debate and substantiating the Marr-Albus theory predictions.

Reviewers note that 'the experiment in Figure 6 is of significant interest, but it is described too briefly' and request quantitation of colocalization and 'some indication of the reproducibility of the results.' While not rejecting the M1-BPN connectivity findings, reviewers indicate the evidence needs strengthening through additional quantitative analysis.

Reviewers state that 'the discussion of the meaning of an internal model, and their statements about how the convergence of corollary discharge onto sensory neurons automatically converts the motor signals to sensory coordinates are not particularly persuasive.' They request discussion of implications for cerebellar learning theory, noting that early convergence means signals 'cannot be adjusted independently by the putative learning mechanisms in the molecular layer.'
